dial.summary: S&P Global Flash PMI surged to a 52-month manufacturing high of 57.0 and a 62-month composite high of 58.4 on September 23, injecting fresh growth optimism ahead of October 1 ISM; DXY edged to 100.74 and real yields held at 2.63% (near 18-year highs), keeping two structural macro headwinds active, but global M2 trending up at $103.6T, Fed balance sheet flat at $6.75T, near-zero BTC funding at ~0.01%, declining stablecoin dominance at 10.2%, and TOTAL crypto rising to $3.02T sustain the BTC Accumulation posture with BTC.D firm at 57.07%.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed near $103.6T as of mid-September 2026 per MacroMicro/StreetStats (6–8 week reporting lag); US M2 reached $23.218T in July 2026 (+5.4% YoY) per MacroRadar — consistent with the G4 aggregate holding near $103.6T; global broad money supply (wider aggregate including all central banks) hit a record $150T in June 2026 (+$10.7T YoY) per spendnode.io, the ninth consecutive monthly record; 4-week trend up confirmed (expansion from ~$103.0T in late August to $103.6T in mid-September, +0.6% over 4 weeks); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); no new G4 aggregate print yet for late September given the 6–8 week reporting lag; next major catalyst is the September 30 PCE and October 1 ISM data cluster.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM Manufacturing releases October 1 — no new ISM data as of September 24; LEADING SIGNAL: S&P Global Flash US Manufacturing PMI for September surged to 57.0 (prior 53.9, a 52-month high) on September 23, suggesting potential ISM upside on October 1; status neutral (ISM above 50 but falling on a 4-week basis; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies to the August ISM read); if October 1 ISM confirms the flash PMI's strength (>55 and rising), status would shift to supportive.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at 100.7450 on September 23, 2026 (up 0.14% on the session, up +1.76% over the past month, up +2.93% over 12 months per Trading Economics); 4-week trend up: ~99.0 (Aug 22–24) → 100.74 (Sep 23) = +1.74%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY remains above the 100 threshold for a second consecutive session; hawkish Fed stance (fed funds 3.75%–4.00% post Sep 16 hike) underpins the USD; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status; DXY above 100 joins real yields at 2.63% as the two active macro headwinds; 30-day DTWEXBGS broad dollar index trend used for trend derivation (correlates closely with ICE DXY spot).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.63% as of September 22, 2026 per WatchGold/CNBC; breakeven inflation rate near 2.26%; 10Y nominal near 4.96% confirms real yield in the 2.62–2.63% range; essentially unchanged from the Sep 21 reading — no new DFII10 data point available for Sep 23 at time of this update (FRED releases Sep 24); eased marginally from the Sep 18 peak of 2.66% (highest 10Y TIPS level since October 2008); 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 22) → 2.63% (Sep 22) = +18bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status to supportive; the S&P Global Flash PMI surge (composite 58.4) may push breakevens higher, adding further pressure.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 23, 2026: 2s10s spread at +0.25% (+25bps) per 24/7 Wall St. / Treasury data — widened 5bps from the September 21 reading of +0.20%; 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 21, pre-FOMC) → +25bps (Sep 23) = −13bps over 4 weeks, as the front end anchors near the 3.75%–4.00% fed funds rate while the long end drifts on growth expectations; status neutral (positive spread but still flattening on a 4-week basis; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening over 4 weeks; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); curve backed away from near-flat readings, but remains narrow by historical standards; October 7 FOMC Minutes release and October 27–28 FOMC are the next key repricing catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747B ($6.747T) for week ending September 16, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 17 (Treasuries $4,554B, MBS $1,914B, other $279B); new H.4.1 for week ending September 23 is scheduled for release September 24 — not yet available at time of this update; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.747T (Sep 16) = +$47B over 4 weeks, marginal expansion within flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity, not new asset purchases); total assets up ~$138B year-on-year; next H.4.1 (week ending Sep 23) expected Thursday September 24.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.0095% per 8h as of September 23–24, 2026 per CoinGlass/MacroMicro (30-day range: consistently sub-0.01% throughout September); near-zero funding during BTC's consolidation confirms the move remains spot-driven, not leveraged-long; BTC dominance at 57.07% with total crypto market cap at $3.02T; 30-day trend flat (funding has remained sub-0.01% throughout September, no regime change); status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; near-zero funding is the ideal BTC Accumulation signal); S&P Global Flash PMI composite 58.4 (5-year high) provides potential growth tailwind for risk asset sentiment heading into the Oct 1 ISM / Oct 2 NFP data cluster.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B (September 24, 2026 per CoinMarketCap/StablecoinBeat); total crypto market cap $3.02T (TOTAL per CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap, +0.38% 24h); stablecoin dominance 10.2% ($308B / $3.02T), down from 10.25% on September 22–23; BTC dominance 57.07%; 30-day trend down: stablecoin dominance peaked at ~13% in Q1 2026 and has declined to 10.2% by late September as capital deployed into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply); USDT ~60.57% (~$183.4B), USDC ~24% of stablecoin market; declining stablecoin dominance alongside firm BTC.D above 57% reinforces the BTC Accumulation thesis; S&P Global Flash PMI surge (composite 58.4) may accelerate rotation from stablecoins into risk assets.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~4.96%, real yields 2.63%) and DXY at 100.74 weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp), though S&P Global Flash PMI new orders surged in September (57.0 manufacturing flash); Q2 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully incorporating the post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) tightening cluster; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched alongside S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) suggesting resilient consumer activity; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — forward-looking consumer sentiment after September's global central bank tightening cluster; S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) released September 23 signals underlying resilience; a sharp decline from August would confirm elevated financing costs (real yields 2.63%, 10Y ~4.96%) are weighing on consumer psychology despite the PMI signal; August PCE print follows the next day on September 30.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — key Fed input for assessing labor market tightness; a significant decline toward 7M openings would signal elevated rates are cooling labor demand; October 27–28 FOMC will weigh this alongside August PCE (Sep 30), September NFP (Oct 2), and October FOMC Minutes (Oct 7).

upcoming.title: Q2 2026 GDP (Third Estimate)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Economic Analysis Q2 2026 GDP third (final) estimate at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside August PCE and ADP; a downward revision would add to recession concerns given the FOMC's hawkish Sep 16 hike and real yields at 2.63%; includes BEA annual updates of national, industry, and regional data; a strong final print confirms the economy can absorb the current rate cycle, consistent with the S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) on September 23.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays report including August 2026 PCE Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; July 2026 PCE was +3.7% YoY; a reading above +3.5% YoY reinforces the FOMC's case for continued tightening ahead of October 27–28; core PCE (ex food and energy) watched most closely; released alongside Q2 GDP third estimate and ADP; the last major inflation print before the October FOMC blackout period begins.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP Research Institute private payrolls estimate for September 2026 at 8:15 AM ET — advance read on labor conditions ahead of official NFP (Oct 2); released alongside Q2 GDP and August PCE on a data-dense final day of September; a strong print (+150K or above) reinforces the NFP-resilient narrative and keeps rate-hike expectations elevated for the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — most consequential ISM read in months; August ISM was 54.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); S&P Global Flash Manufacturing PMI surged to 57.0 (52-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal; an ISM print above 55 and rising would shift the ISM indicator to supportive status; a move below 50 would signal contraction; completes the September manufacturing picture started by the September 23 flash estimate.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 26, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 26, 2026 — second consecutive weekly read post-FOMC tightening; released same day as ISM Manufacturing PMI; a back-to-back rise in claims would be an early signal that cumulative rate tightening (fed funds 3.75%–4.00%) is beginning to bite on employment; prior weeks approximately 206K.
